skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Search, download, and analyze NCBI GEO gene expression datasets with GEOparse, Biopython Entrez, and workflow guidance for transcriptomics research.
skill.summary: Find and process NCBI GEO expression studies for transcriptomics workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static scanner over-reported many Markdown code fence, identifier, and placeholder patterns. I confirmed only the FTP transport findings because the skill documents unauthenticated ftp:// downloads from NCBI; no prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace ftp:// examples and ftplib.FTP guidance with HTTPS options when available, or require checksum verification after downloads.

remediation.issue: API key shown as an inline placeholder
remediation.suggestion: Show loading the optional NCBI API key from an environment variable or a local secret store instead of assigning a literal string.

remediation.issue: Bulk download guidance can consume large disk space
remediation.suggestion: Recommend file-size checks, explicit destination directories, and user confirmation before recursive or large supplementary downloads.

content.value_statement: Researchers need reliable access to public gene expression studies before analysis. This skill guides GEO search, download, metadata review, and transcriptomics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains GEO accession types, including GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and profiles.
Provides search workflows for GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles through Biopython Entrez.
Shows how to retrieve GEO series, samples, platforms, matrices, SOFT files, and supplementary files.
Covers GEOparse workflows for metadata extraction, expression matrices, and local caching.
Outlines quality control, differential expression, clustering, and meta-analysis workflows.
Documents GEO file formats, FTP directory structure, rate limits, and citation practices.
limitations: Depends on NCBI service availability, GEO record quality, and programmatic access limits.
Large series and supplementary files may require significant disk space and download time.
Metadata, platform annotations, and expression normalization can vary across submissions.
Statistical results require review by a qualified bioinformatics or domain expert.

use_cases.title: Find datasets for a research question
use_cases.description: Search GEO by organism, disease, technology, author, date, or accession and compare candidate studies.

use_cases.title: Prepare expression data for analysis
use_cases.description: Download series metadata, sample tables, platform annotations, and expression matrices into a local workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan cross-study transcriptomics work
use_cases.description: Review platform differences, sample metadata, gene mapping, and batch risks before meta-analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant GEO Studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public GEO studies for [condition] in [organism]. Return accession IDs, titles, sample counts, platforms, and GEO record links.

prompt_templates.title: Download One GEO Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Download metadata and the expression matrix for [GSE accession] with GEOparse. Save files under [directory] and summarize sample groups.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Treatment Effects
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare control and treatment samples in [GSE accession]. Explain normalization checks, differential expression steps, and outputs for significant genes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Meta-Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a reproducible meta-analysis plan for these GEO series: [accessions]. Include platform harmonization, gene mapping, batch considerations, and citation checks.

output_examples.input: Find human breast cancer GEO studies with available expression matrices.
output: Candidate series are grouped by accession, organism, platform, sample count, and publication metadata.
The response notes which records have series matrix files and which require supplementary downloads.
The workflow identifies required Python libraries, the target data directory, expected GEO files, and metadata checks.
It also flags file size, sample grouping, platform annotation, and normalization questions before analysis.

output_examples.input: Plan a meta-analysis across three GEO studies for TP53 expression.
output: The plan covers accession validation, platform compatibility, probe-to-gene mapping, expression extraction, and batch-effect review.
It includes citation reminders and a clear list of assumptions that need manual confirmation.

best_practices: Set an Entrez email and respect NCBI rate limits for every automated query.
Validate sample metadata, platform annotations, and expression scale before statistical analysis.
Record accession IDs, download dates, software versions, and source citations for reproducibility.
anti_patterns: Downloading entire directories before checking file sizes and available disk space.
Assuming GEO expression values are normalized without reviewing submission metadata.
Combining studies from different platforms without gene mapping and batch-effect controls.

faq.question: What is NCBI GEO?
faq.answer: GEO is a public repository for functional genomics data, including microarray and sequencing studies.

faq.question: Does this skill download data automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and commands. The user or agent must choose what to run and where to store files.

faq.question: Which GEO accession types are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Series, Samples, Platforms, curated DataSets, and GEO Profiles.

faq.question: Can it analyze RNA-seq data?
faq.answer: It can help locate RNA-seq studies and retrieve metadata, but raw RNA-seq processing may need separate tools.

faq.question: What Python libraries does it use?
faq.answer: Examples use GEOparse for GEO records and Biopython Entrez for NCBI E-utilities queries.

faq.question: How should I handle large datasets?
faq.answer: Check file sizes first, plan disk space, download incrementally, and cache data in a clear project directory.
